records.title: Introduction to Marine Life

records.text: B BIO 130 Introduction to Marine Life (5) NSc Identification of invertebrates, fish, mammals, and birds of the Salish Sea with a focus on their anatomy, adaptations, and roles in the ecosystem. records.text: B BIO 180 Introductory Biology I (5) NSc For students intending to take advanced courses in the biological sciences or enroll in pre-professional programs. records.header: B BIO 231 Genes, Genomes and Heredity (5) SSc/NSc
records.text: B BIO 231 Genes, Genomes and Heredity (5) SSc/NSc Explores basic concepts of heredity, including DNA structure and function, Mendel's rules of inheritance, and human genetic diseases. Goals include understanding current issues in the field, including genetic screening and testing, DNA fingerprinting and forensic analysis, the genetic basis of cancer, and genetically modified organisms. Offered: jointly with BISSTS 231.

records.text: B BIO 233 Cancer: Biology, Risk, and Treatment (5) NSc Addresses the basic biology of cancer, genetic and environmental risk factors, and treatment options. Prerequisite: minimum grade of 2.0 in either B CHEM 115 or B CHEM 143/B CHEM 144.

records.header: B BIO 260 The Diversity of Sex (5) NSc, DIV
records.text: B BIO 260 The Diversity of Sex (5) NSc, DIV Explores the diversity and complexity of sex across animal species, including humans, using a comparative and evolutionary approach. Recommended: B BIO 180 or BIOL 180. Offered: Sp.

records.header: B BIO 310 Brain and Behavior (5) NSc
records.text: B BIO 310 Brain and Behavior (5) NSc Interdisciplinary exploration of the biological basis of human behavior, including altruism, aggression, learning, communication, and mating. Draws on neuroanatomy, neuroscience, endocrinology, ethology, genetics, and sociobiology to examine how the brain influences, and is influenced, by behavior. Readings include primary literature as well as popular publications. Course overlaps with: TPSYCH 260/T BIOL 260. Offered: Sp.

records.header: B BIO 320 Behavioral Neuroscience (5) NSc
records.text: B BIO 320 Behavioral Neuroscience (5) NSc An exploration of how brain cells and their connections form functional neural networks to control and modulate behavior in both humans and non-human animals. Takes both bottom-up and top-down approaches to understand how the nervous system facilitates, regulates, and modulates sensation and perception, muscle movement, vision, learning and memory, wanting and liking, drug addiction, and belief. Course equivalent to: T BIOL 412. Course overlaps with: NEUSCI 302. Prerequisite: B BIO 220. Offered: W.
